properties.rationale: A detection-only candidate identifies prometheus-metrics at this path. The endpoint might expose operational information without authorization. properties.title: Potential public directory listing or unintended file disclosure
properties.rationale: The recorded /ftp path returned HTTP 200. Its name suggests a file-distribution surface that might expose a directory listing or files intended to remain private. No listing, file contents, or authorization requirements are recorded; the response could also be an application fallback. The impact estimate assumes limited unintended disclosure.

properties.title: Potential sensitive information embedded in a client-side bundle
properties.rationale: The crawl recorded /main.js alongside several JavaScript chunks, making client-delivered code an evidenced inspection surface. This bundle might contain nonpublic configuration or other information unintentionally shipped to clients. No bundle contents or exposed secrets are recorded, and ordinary public route names would not by themselves establish a vulnerability.

properties.title: Potential overly permissive cross-origin access
properties.rationale: The fingerprint records an Access-Control-Allow-Origin header but omits its value and any credential-related headers. The root response might permit an untrusted origin to read information that should be restricted. Header presence alone is not a vulnerability: this hypothesis requires both permissive browser-enforced cross-origin behavior and sensitive response content, neither of which is recorded. The impact estimate is conditional on limited sensitive disclosure.

properties.title: Risk to verify: public Prometheus metrics exposure
properties.fix: No disclosure was confirmed; the supplied testing summaries conflict. If /metrics is publicly reachable, remove its public application route or deny /metrics and /metrics/ at the public reverse proxy. Expose metrics only on an internal listener restricted to the Prometheus collector, with authentication enforced before serving metrics.
properties.detection: At the public ingress, alert on requests whose normalized path is /metrics or begins /metrics/ from sources outside the approved monitoring network. Include method, path, status, source address, and authenticated identity. Treat a 200 response to an unauthenticated external request as a priority validation signal, not proof of sensitive disclosure.

properties.title: Risk to verify: directory listing or unintended files under /ftp
properties.fix: No listing or file disclosure was confirmed. If /ftp is not a required public feature, remove its static-directory mount and deny /ftp and /ftp/ descendants at the public ingress. If downloads are required, replace directory serving with an explicit allowlist of public files; keep all other files outside the served directory and disable directory indexing. Disabling indexing alone does not prevent direct downloads.
properties.detection: Alert on requests to /ftp or its descendants when this route is disabled. If public downloads remain enabled, alert on requests for paths outside the published allowlist, especially backup, configuration, dotfile, or archive names. Escalate successful responses for non-allowlisted paths and bursts of distinct filename probes.

properties.title: Risk to verify: sensitive content in the client bundle
properties.fix: No sensitive bundle content was confirmed, and no source scan was supplied. Inspect the deployed /main.js and associated source maps. If credentials, private keys, or confidential configuration are present, remove them from frontend source and build-time substitutions, store them in backend-only configuration, and perform privileged operations through authenticated, authorized backend endpoints. Rebuild and redeploy the bundle, purge cached copies, and revoke or rotate any exposed credentials. Add a secret-scanning gate for generated frontend artifacts before deployment.
properties.detection: Fail the frontend artifact gate on verified secret patterns in generated JavaScript or source maps, recording artifact names and redacted locations rather than secret values. Normal /main.js downloads cannot reliably distinguish exploitation from ordinary browsing; correlate suspected exposure with anomalous use of affected credentials in backend or provider audit logs.

properties.title: Risk to verify: overly permissive CORS
properties.fix: No exploitable cross-origin access was confirmed. If the application requires only same-origin browser access, disable CORS middleware and remove Access-Control-Allow-* response headers. Otherwise, configure an exact allowlist of required origins including scheme, hostname, and port; do not reflect arbitrary Origin values or accept null. Emit Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true only where credentialed cross-origin access is necessary, limit allowed methods and headers, and add Vary: Origin when responses vary by origin. Apply this policy to sensitive API routes as well as /.
properties.detection: Log the request Origin and response Access-Control-Allow-Origin and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials headers on relevant routes. Alert when an origin outside the approved list is echoed as allowed, especially with credentials enabled. Also flag wildcard origin responses on endpoints designated as sensitive. An unapproved Origin request alone is a probe, not evidence that a browser could read the response.
